title: Perseverance was lowered onto Mars on cables from a hovering rocket jetpack

cover.alt: Two camera views during Perseverance’s landing: above, the descent stage’s rocket nozzles seen from the rover; below, the rover hanging on three cables over brown Martian ground.

body: Perseverance weighs about **1,025 kg**, far too heavy for the airbags that let earlier rovers bounce to a stop. So its descent stage, a platform with eight rocket engines, slowed to about 2.7 km/h some 20 m above the ground and lowered the rover on cables about 6.4 m long. Once the rover confirmed touchdown, the stage let go of the cables and flew off to crash at a safe distance. Curiosity, the first rover to use the sky crane, had landed the same way.

slides.alt: Split view of Perseverance’s landing: the top camera looks up at the descent stage’s rocket nozzles and cables; the bottom camera looks down at the rover hanging on cables until dust billows up around it.
slides.caption: 18 February 2021: the rover looks up at its descent stage (top) as the stage looks down and lowers it on cables (bottom), until dust boils up at touchdown.
slides.music: “Drums of the Deep” Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com) · CC BY 4.0

slides.prompt: Earlier Mars rovers bounced to a stop inside giant airbags. Why couldn’t Perseverance?
slides.detail: Even Curiosity, at nearly 900 kg, was too much: airbags big enough to cushion it would have been too heavy to launch.

steps.label: A parachute slows the falling capsule
Rover and rocket stage drop free and fire
20 m up, the rover is lowered on cables
Wheels touch; the cables are released
The stage flies off and crashes far away

slides.note: Length of the landing ellipse; Perseverance’s was 7.7 by 6.6 km

slides.question: What did Perseverance’s rocket stage do once it had set the rover down?
options: Landed beside it as a weather station
Flew off to crash at a safe distance
Hovered overhead as a radio relay
Climbed back into orbit around Mars
slides.explanation: After letting go of the cables it flew away, so that its crash could not damage the rover. Curiosity’s descent stage came down about 650 m from the rover.
